newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC to sign Brunei refinery deal.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC to sign Brunei refinery deal.

text.p: Taiwan's state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp will sign a memorandum of understanding with Brunei on July 23 to build a refinery there with a daily capacity of 50,000-60,000 barrels, company officials said on Tuesday.
The memorandum would be signed by Chinese Petroleum Chairman Lee Shu-chiu and senior Brunei government officials.
"The (CPC) chairman will visit our Singapore office on July 17 and go to Brunei to sign the refinery memorandum on July 23," a senior Chinese Petroleum official told Reuters.
The official estimated the joint-venture at US$1 billion, but declined to give further details.

The oil-rich Brunei currently has only one small refinery with a daily capacity of just 9,000 barrels. The refinery is operated by Brunei Shell Petroleum Co Bhd., an equally owned joint venture between Royal/Dutch Shell and the Brunei government.
In May, Brunei's Oil and Gas Agency signed a letter of intent with state-owned German engineering company IAB to build a 160,000 barrel-per-day refinery at cost of 2.6 billion marks (US$1.5 billion).
IAB has said a feasibility study for the project would be completed by the end of 1997 and construction would take 4-1/2 years.
In 1996, Brunei produced about 165,000 barrels per day of crude oil and has proven reserves of 1.4 billion barrels.
Chinese Petroleum declined to comment whether its plan was related to the German project.
